fix.notes: Pure JS refactor — moves object construction from per-call to module load time. No behaviour change; the formatter options and post-processing replace() chain are unchanged. No Python unit tests cover this JS file.
fix.pr_body:
## What was wrong

`PD.formatPercentage` in `shared_web/static/js/pd.js` constructed a new `Intl.NumberFormat` object on every call. The MDN docs note that constructing these formatters repeatedly is inefficient — the object should be reused.

## What changed

Extracted the `Intl.NumberFormat` construction to a module-level constant `PD_PERCENTAGE_FORMATTER` (3 lines added before `PD.formatPercentage`). The function body is replaced with a single `PD_PERCENTAGE_FORMATTER.format(value)` call; the existing `.replace()` chain is unchanged.

## Validation

`uv run --frozen python dev.py lint` passed. This is a pure JS refactor with no logic change — the formatter options, the `.replace()` chain, and the output are all identical to before.

Fixes #12540

tests.detail: All checks passed — JS-only change, no Python unit tests applicable

evidence.detail: PD.formatPercentage creates a new Intl.NumberFormat(...) object on every invocation rather than reusing a cached instance — MDN explicitly warns this pattern is inefficient for repeated calls
Format tick marks for percentages in a sane fashion — introduced PD.formatPercentage using Intl.NumberFormat but still constructs a new instance per call
formatPercentage is used as a Chart.js tick callback and tooltip formatter, meaning it is called once per data point per render — potentially dozens of times per chart

triage.fix_sketch: In shared_web/static/js/pd.js, extract the Intl.NumberFormat construction to a module-level constant: const PD_PERCENTAGE_FORMATTER = new Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, { style: 'percent', minimumSignificantDigits: 2, maximumSignificantDigits: 2 }); then replace the new Intl.NumberFormat(...) inside formatPercentage with PD_PERCENTAGE_FORMATTER.format(value) — keeping the existing .replace() chain unchanged. 3-line net change.
